claims.text: The 1878 treaty distinguishes Bosnia’s occupation from Serbia’s conditional recognition. Serbia’s later constitution describes its own joint lawmaking, not Bosnia’s institution. The acquired retrospectives separately identify Bosnia’s council, transfer and Šola government before the Belgrade union address. These are actual institutional links rather than a deduction from war or a single label. The museum’s unelected-committee qualification and conflicting membership counts prevent a universal-consent inference. Original acts remain uncollated.
